mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10Y-2Y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, as measured by the year-over-year change in the INDPRO index, signals a supply shock that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following a -2% YoY drop in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid rise in the unemployment rate, defined as a 0.5 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a weakening labor market that will negatively impact consumer spending and drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (Conference Board index) rises by > 5 points during the signal period, indicating that the labor market weakening is temporary and not a major concern for consumers.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the federal funds rate, defined as a 1 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, signals a tightening monetary policy that will negatively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a 1pp increase in FEDFUNDS over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in housing starts, as measured by the year-over-year change in the HOUST index, signals a strengthening housing market that will boost consumer spending and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 30-year mortgage rates rise by > 1pp during the signal period, indicating that the housing market strength is likely to be short-lived.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid decrease in the unemployment rate, as measured by a 0.5 percentage point drop over the past 3 months, signals a tightening labor market that will boost wage growth and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Average hourly earnings growth slows by > 0.5pp during the signal period, indicating that the labor market tightening is not translating into wage growth.

mechanism_narrative: When both real GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) are accelerating, as measured by their respective year-over-year changes, this signals a broad-based strengthening of the economy that will drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve flattens by > 50 bps during the signal period, indicating that the economic strength may be short-lived and a recession may be looming.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is rising rapidly, as measured by a 1 percentage point increase over the past 3 months, and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is simultaneously rising, this signals a toxic combination of tightening monetary policy and labor market weakness that will drive negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 1pp in 3 months AND UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 3 months
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following the joint trigger condition.
